title: The water board in five minutes

steps.title: Where the money is
steps.body: {{summary:Outstanding}} is owed, and {{summary:Overdue}} of it is overdue. Every figure is added up by the database, not typed.

steps.title: The oldest debt is the biggest
steps.body: Bills more than 180 days old: {{group:Over 180 days}}. Open the group to see who owes it.

steps.title: A customer's statement
steps.body: What they owe, how late, what they hold on account, and below it every bill, payment and case. One page, no report to run.

steps.title: Every change, on the record
steps.body: Who changed what and when. Nobody can edit it, not even a Manager.

steps.title: A write-off needs a second pair of eyes
steps.body: Whoever asks for it can't approve it, and above the limit a second Manager has to as well. The approval is on the record too.

steps.title: Your cases, and only yours
steps.body: A Recovery officer sees the cases they own. Another officer's case isn't just hidden: for them it doesn't exist.

steps.title: Hand out work in one move
steps.body: Tick the cases that need an owner and assign them together: all or none, each one audited.

steps.title: See it as someone else
steps.body: Choose View as role to see exactly what a Recovery officer sees. Their cases, nothing more. The same rules the server enforces.

ending: What Clicker did that you did not have to: age every bill, allocate every payment to the oldest debt first, and keep each person to what their role allows.
